title: Cap. IX Corvini Arg. 1: as God damns the gospel-contumacious in time, so he reprobated them from eternity
pass_a_gloss: Chapter IX. The arguments of Corvinus are proposed and dissolved. The adversaries therefore are wont to argue from the very decree of damning unto the act or decree of reprobation, in this manner: In what manner considered God damns in time, in such manner considered he decreed to damn, and reprobated from eternity. But he damns men considered as contumacious unto the Gospel, that is, as finally impenitent and unbelieving: Therefore he also reprobated them so considered.
pass_b_english: Chapter IX — Corvinus's arguments proposed and dissolved. Adversaries commonly argue from the decree of damning to the act or decree of reprobation thus: In whatever manner of consideration God damns in time, in that same manner he decreed to damn and reprobated from eternity. But he damns men considered as contumacious to the Gospel — that is, as finally impenitent and unbelieving. Therefore he also reprobated them so considered.
source_text: Cap. IX. Corvini argumenta proponuntur et diluuntur. Argumentari igitur solent adversarii ab ipso damnandi decreto ad actum sive decretum reprobationis, hoc modo: Qualiter consideratos Deus damnat in tempore, taliter consideratos decrevit damnare, et reprobavit ab aeterno. Sed damnat homines consideratos ut Evangelio immorigeros, hoc est, ut finaliter impenitentes et incredulos: Ergo etiam taliter consideratos reprobavit.
